battle.name: 隋平建國門事變
battle.brief: 大業六年（610）夏曆正月初一拂曉，數十名白衣白冠、自稱彌勒佛的壯士焚香持花，闖入洛陽皇城建國門（端門）。監門官與守門官軍叩頭禮拜，兵器為其所奪，與齊王楊暕衛兵互鬥，壯士全滅。隋煬帝當日下令大索京師，連坐者千餘家。卡面羅馬重步兵不在此戰，可比者為隋軍環首刀與長槊。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這不是兩國之間的戰爭，而是隋朝大業六年正月初一發生在東都洛陽皇城門前的一次失敗的宮禁滲透與起事未遂，交戰的兩方分屬同一國家體制的內外。起事的一方是數十名民間壯士：他們白衣白冠，焚香持花，自稱彌勒佛，以彌勒出世的名義號召，目標是端門之內的宮禁。壯士背後並無諸侯或外國勢力，只有大業年間在關中、關東與江南民間廣泛流傳的彌勒信仰網絡，以及在隋律嚴禁造妖書與禁斷彌勒之後仍然存在的秘密結社與私抄的經卷。鎮壓的一方是隋朝中央的整套機構：皇城內的武衛、翊衛宿衛，端門的監門官與守門官軍，齊王楊暕在洛陽的親王府衛兵，以及事後奉詔搜索京師的洛陽府與各州縣官署，加上刑部、御史台派出的推鞫官員。沒有任何外敵介入，沒有盟軍，也沒有外交事件；這是一場王朝以國家機器對付一批民間武裝的鎮壓。放在國際層面上看，同一年的隋朝正把注意力全部放在西面：車駕西巡，經劍門入蜀，渡青海，至張掖，於焉支山受西域二十七國使臣朝見；與此同時，北方與突厥的邊線維持在脆弱的停戰狀態。洛陽門前這場短促的交鋒，與西巡所象徵的對外經營，恰好是同一件事的兩面。
countriesEn: This was not a war between two states but a failed attempt to storm a palace gate in the Eastern Capital of Luoyang on the first day of the first month of the sixth year of Daye, and both sides belonged to the inner and outer parts of a single polity. The rising side was a few dozen armed men from the towns: dressed in white with white caps, carrying burning incense and flowers, and calling themselves Maitreya, they raised the coming of Maitreya as the banner under which they acted, and their aim was the palace precincts behind the Duan Gate. Behind the men there was no lord and no foreign power, only the network of Maitreya belief that had spread widely among the common people of Guanzhong, Guandong and Jiangnan during the Daye years, together with the secret societies and the privately copied sutras that survived the Sui court's ban on Maitreya teaching and on the forging of demonic writings. The side that suppressed them was the entire machinery of the Sui state: the Wuwei and Yiwei guards of the palace, the gate supervisor and the soldiers who kept the Duan Gate, the household guard of Prince Qi Yang Jian in Luoyang, and afterwards the officials of Luoyang Prefecture and of the commanderies and counties who searched the capital on imperial order, together with the judicial and censorate officials who handled the cases. No foreign enemy was involved, there was no allied force and no diplomatic incident; this was a dynasty bringing the weight of the state to bear on a band of armed townsmen. On the international level, the Sui in that very year had all its attention turned westward: the imperial carriage went on the western tour, entered Shu by way of Jiange, crossed Qinghai, reached Zhangye and received the envoys of the twenty-seven states of the Western Regions at Yanzhi Mountain; at the same time the northern line against the Turks was held in a fragile truce. The short clash at the gate of Luoyang and the reach abroad advertised by that tour are two faces of the same thing.
people: 留下姓名的只有皇帝和齊王，其餘多是身分而不是名字。隋煬帝楊廣是全案的決策者：大業六年正月車駕將西巡劍門，他在正月初一得到端門被闖入的報告，下令在洛陽全城搜索，並准許以連坐的方式追查，牽連者達千餘家。齊王楊暕是隋文帝之孫、晉王楊俊之子，大業年間封齊王、兼河南道行台尚書令，以書法與文才見稱，詔令常出其手；事發當日他的王府衛兵恰在皇城一帶巡行，與闖門的壯士相遇互鬥，成為直接扭轉局面的一支力量。監門官與守門官軍在史籍中沒有留下姓名，只留下他們的動作：叩頭禮拜，兵器被繳；這是整份記載中最沉痛的一筆，因為它說明皇城門禁在那一刻不是防線，而是通道。壯士的首領同樣無名，連人數也只以「數十」概之，無從得知他們如何籌劃、是否另有內應。背景中還有兩位與事變無直接關係、卻決定了當年氣候的人物：一是主持西域經營的裴矩，其所著《西域圖記》正是西巡的知識支撐；二是占驗與讖緯在隋廷的份量——彌勒佛出世本屬釋迦牟尼佛衰、彌勒佛代興的教義說法，能在宮門前變成行動口號，靠的正是民間對這套說法的長期信仰。
peopleEn: Only the emperor and Prince Qi are named; everyone else survives as a status rather than as a name. The Sui Yangdi, Yang Guang, was the man who decided the case: in the first month of the sixth year of Daye, with the imperial carriage about to depart on the western tour to Jiange, he was told that the Duan Gate had been forced, he ordered a thorough search of all Luoyang, and he allowed the case to be pursued by collective implication, so that more than a thousand households were drawn in. Prince Qi Yang Jian was a grandson of Emperor Wen and a son of Prince Jin Yang Jun; in the Daye years he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi and held the office of Director of the Henan Circuit, and he was known for his calligraphy and his literary talent, with many edicts passing through his hand. On the day in question his household guard happened to be patrolling near the palace, met the men who had forced the gate, and fought them, and it was this body of men that turned the situation. The gate supervisor and the soldiers who kept the gate are left in the histories without names, and only their actions survive: bowing their heads in worship and having their weapons taken from them. That is the most painful line in the whole account, for it shows that the palace guard at that moment was not a line of defence but a passageway. The leader of the intruders is equally nameless, and even their number is given only as several dozen; nothing records how they planned or whether they had a second party inside. Two further figures belong to the background of the year without being directly involved: Pei Ju, who directed Sui policy in the western regions and whose Xiyu Tuji was the intellectual scaffolding of the western tour; and the place of divination and prophecy at the Sui court, for the doctrine that Maitreya would succeed a declining Shakyamuni could turn into a slogan at a palace gate only because ordinary people had believed in it for a long time.
kits: 卡面所配的羅馬重步兵並沒有出現在大業六年的洛陽，這點必須先講清楚：這場衝突裡的實際裝備全部是隋制，羅馬重步兵只能作為一件對照物，用來看兩套體系各自怎樣理解「守門」。羅馬重步兵的標準配備是分段鎧甲、大盾、重標槍與短劍：鎧甲由橫排鐵片以皮條連綴，肩、軀幹與腰際分段可活動；大盾是半圓形曲面的木盾，蒙皮包邊，釘有金屬飾件；長矛手先拋出重標槍，其刃狹長、頸部細而軟，落地後前段折斷，只留一截插在盾前的殘柄；近身時換短劍刺擊。它所在的軍團以百人隊為骨、輔以輔助兵，野戰靠三列縱深與陣中相互掩護，攻守的節奏由投石、角號與嚴格的結營秩序維持；卡面所說那句話正是這套體系的要旨——羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。落到洛陽端門前，隋代宮禁的裝備邏輯完全不同。守門與宿衛的近身兵器是環首直刃刀與長槊、馬槊：前者刀身直脊直刃、單面開鋒、柄端作圓環，隋唐墓葬與佛窟壁畫所見即是此制；雙刃的劍在隋代更多作儀飾與佩用，並非野戰主力。防護上是明光鎧、札甲與兜鍪，手持棗木或柳葉形盾，弓弩以角弓、木弓與臂弩、蹶張弩為主，皇城門樓上還架設防禦用的固定機弩。糧秣方面，隋代靠的是江南漕運與洛陽的大倉，米粟經永濟渠北運，軍隊的續戰能力繫於船與河，而不是繫於重甲。武器看來輕，補給線卻比羅馬軍團更長，這正是隋朝真正的弱點。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card face did not appear at Luoyang in the sixth year of Daye, and that has to be said first: everything actually used in this clash was of Sui make, and the legionary can only serve as a comparison, useful for seeing how two systems each understood the problem of holding a gate. The standard kit of a Roman legionary was segmented armour, a large shield, a heavy javelin and a short sword. The armour was made of iron strips arranged in horizontal rows and linked by leather thongs, articulated at the shoulder, the torso and the waist. The shield was a semicircular curved wooden scutum, edged in leather and studded with metal fittings. The pilum was thrown by the front ranks; its blade was long and narrow and its shank thin and soft, so that on landing the front section folded away and left only a socketed remnant standing in the ground before the enemy shield wall. At close quarters the gladius took over. The unit structure rested on the centuria, reinforced by auxiliaries; in the field it advanced in three-line depth with mutual covering between the lines, and the rhythm of attack and defence was kept up by artillery, signal horns and the strict order of the marching camp. The sentence on the card states the point of that system exactly: Roman strength rested on the replenishment of manpower and on supply lines, not on heavy equipment. At the Duan Gate in Luoyang the logic of Sui palace equipment was entirely different. The close weapons of the gate guards and the palace watch were the ring-pommel dao and the long shao and cavalry lance: the dao has a straight spine, a straight single-edged blade and a ring at the pommel, exactly as the knives excavated from Sui and Tang tombs and shown in the murals of the Buddhist caves reveal; the double-edged sword in the Sui period was more often ceremonial and personal wear than a weapon of the line. For protection there were Mingguang plate and lamellar armour and steel helmets, with jujube-wood or willow-leaf shields; bows and crossbows were horn bows, wooden bows, arm bows and the powerful foot-held crossbow, and the gate towers of the imperial city carried fixed crossbows for the defence of the wall. Supply was another matter: the Sui drew it from the grain transport of the south and the great granaries of Luoyang, with rice and millet brought north by the Yongji canal, and the ability of an army to keep fighting was tied to boats and rivers rather than to heavy armour. The weapons looked lighter; the supply line was longer than that of a Roman legion. That, in the end, was the real weakness of the Sui.
tactics: 起事方的戰術只有兩步：第一步是偽裝與奇襲——白衣白冠，焚香持花，自稱彌勒佛，這一身行頭同時做三件事：表明宗教身分、說明自己是不日當興的新佛之徒、用香與花製造一種不需動武的合法性。守門者先是叩頭禮拜，等於主動放棄抵抗；壯士隨即奪取衛兵的兵器，用繳來的武器武裝自己，這是全案最關鍵的一個動作。第二步是向宮內推進：只要再穿過一道門、進入皇城朝會之所，憑著「彌勒代興」的口號便可能裹挾宮中不滿現狀的人。鎮壓方靠的卻是位置與制度：齊王楊暕的衛兵正在附近巡行，兩股人馬在門前的空地上短兵相接，用繳來的兵器對上王府的甲兵，壯士人數既少，又沒有真正的指揮與配合，遂一齊戰死。事後的作戰換成行政手段：全城搜索、按戶緝查、以連坐製造震懾。這套處置與羅馬軍團的守備邏輯恰成對照——羅馬的營壘靠方陣、壕溝與嚴格的崗哨輪值，兵源的補充靠退役老兵與盟邦徵召，糧食靠海運小麥與行軍帳；隋廷的端門只有一名監門官與一批守門官軍，武器存放在門樓之下而不是握在手中，門禁的失效不在於兇猛不足，而在於備而不用與人心已潰。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the rising side had only two steps. The first was disguise and surprise: white clothes and white caps, burning incense and flowers, the claim to be Maitreya. That outfit did three things at once, for it announced a religious identity, explained that the men were followers of a new Buddha soon to rise, and used the incense and the flowers to manufacture a legitimacy that required no violence. The guards on duty first bowed their heads in worship, which amounted to giving up resistance voluntarily; the intruders then took the weapons of the soldiers, arming themselves from what they had seized, and this was the single most decisive action of the whole affair. The second step was to push on into the palace: with one more gate crossed and the hall of audience reached, the cry of Maitreya to succeed might have carried along whoever inside was dissatisfied with things as they were. The suppression, by contrast, rested on position and institution. The household guard of Prince Qi Yang Jian was patrolling close by, and the two bodies met in the open space before the gate, weapons taken from the palace guard fighting the armed men of a prince's household. The intruders were few in number, without genuine command or coordination, and were killed to the last man. The measures after that were administrative instead: a search of the whole city, arrest house by house, and collective implication used to produce terror. The contrast with the garrison logic of the Roman legion is exact. Roman camps were rectangles of trench and rampart with strict watch rotations, manning was replenished from discharged veterans and from levies of allied communities, and grain came by sea-borne wheat and by the marching tent; the Duan Gate had a single gate supervisor and a body of gate soldiers, with the weapons lying in the gate tower rather than in men's hands. The failure of the palace guard was not a shortage of ferocity but the difference between arms that are ready and arms that are not, and between men who obey and men whose morale has already broken.
data: 可核的數字不多，但有幾條相當硬。大業六年即西元610年，隋煬帝即位第七年；隋朝自581年建國，至此不過三十年。事發時間是夏曆正月初一，公曆約在同年二月初，且在拂曉之前；起事者的人數記為「數十」，確數無從得知。連坐的規模是「千餘家」——這是史籍肯認的數字，說明搜索牽連的面遠大於端門前的實際交戰規模。洛陽城的尺度可以對照：隋唐洛陽外郭城周長約六十七公里，合一百三十五里左右，是當時亞洲最大的城市之一，極盛時城內人口以百萬計；端門是皇城南面正中的大門，門道開闊，皇城與宮城南北相對，車駕出入與朝會皆在此處，位置上正是一旦被突破便直抵內廷的要衝。當年西巡的護駕與輜重規模，文獻只說沿途供帳如雲而未留下可核的數目；真正留下明確數字的是三年後的大業八年征高句麗，會師之眾達百十三萬、糧資稱是，那一筆不應被移用到本年。隋末戶口的崩落則是另一組可用的背景數字：隋朝極盛時（大業初年）天下約八百九十萬戶，到隋末只剩四百六十萬戶，減幅約半。戰損完全無數：起事者全滅是唯一確定的結果，雙方傷亡人數、被繳械的守門官軍數目、涉案者事後的處分人數，文獻皆無記載。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked, but several of them are hard. The sixth year of Daye is 610 CE, the seventh year of the reign of the Sui Yangdi; the dynasty had been founded in 581 and was not yet thirty years old. The event falls on the first day of the first month of the Sui calendar, corresponding to about the beginning of February 610 in the Gregorian reckoning, and it happened before dawn. The number of the intruders is given as several dozen, and the exact figure cannot be known. The scale of the arrests is the more than a thousand households, the one figure the histories vouch for, and it shows that the sweep reached far beyond the scale of the actual fighting at the gate. The size of Luoyang can be set against it: the outer city of the Sui-Tang Luoyang had a circuit of about sixty-seven kilometres, some one hundred and thirty-five li, and was among the largest cities in Asia, with a population in the hundreds of thousands at its height and in the millions at the peak of the age; the Duan Gate was the great gate on the central axis of the south side of the imperial city, broad in its passages, with the palace city lying to the north, and it was the place through which the imperial carriage passed in and out and where the audiences were held, positionally the very point whose breach would have led straight to the inner court. The scale of the entourage and the baggage train on that year's western tour is given in no checkable number, the records saying only that the supplies along the road were like clouds; the one large figure that survives belongs to the campaign against Goguryeo three years later, in the eighth year of Daye, when a hundred and thirteen thousand men mustered and the provisions were said to match, and it should not be transferred to this year. The collapse of the registered households of the Sui supplies the other background number: from about eight hundred and ninety thousand households at the height of the dynasty, in the early Daye years, the number had fallen to four hundred and sixty thousand by the end, a loss of about half. There is no figure for the fighting at all: the total destruction of the intruders is the only outcome that can be stated, and the numbers of casualties on either side, the number of gate soldiers disarmed and the number of those finally punished in the arrests have no record.
cause: 為什麼會在正月初一拂曉發生這樣一件事，可以從四層去看。最深的一層是隋朝統治的信用正在失效：大業年間連年用兵、大興土木、三征高句麗，徭役與兵役同時壓在關中關東的丁口上，隋末戶口較隋朝極盛時減半已是後果；百姓在這種處境下，把「彌勒佛出世、釋迦牟尼佛衰落」這套從來只存在於經卷與僧徒口耳中的說法，轉成了可以付諸行動的期待。第二層是彌勒信仰的傳播本身：隋文帝在位時曾下禁令，禁斷彌勒教與「造妖書」，但禁而不絕，至大業年間，州縣之中多奉彌勒像，民間抄寫彌勒經、結社相應的情形已非少數，敦煌出土的隋代寫經與文書正是這條線索的實物。第三層是時機：正月初一車駕將發洛陽西巡劍門，皇城要進行大朝會與出行前的種種儀仗調度，端門一線的崗哨、兵器庫與傳令的次序都在最緊密的時候被攪動，守軍的注意力被引向宮中與車馬；同時「新年首日」在民間觀念中意味著舊歲已去、新歲將立，劫難與更替的想像最容易在這樣的日子被點燃。第四層是防線本身的樣子：端門有監門官、有守門官軍、有兵仗，制度上並不缺人缺械，但門禁的運作依賴服從而不是依賴警戒；守門者在宗教口號前叩頭的那一刻，等於整套門禁在最需要它的時刻交出了自己。
causeEn: Why such a thing should have happened before dawn on the first day of the first month can be read at four levels. The deepest is the failing credit of Sui government. The Daye years brought continuous campaigns, enormous construction projects and the three expeditions against Goguryeo, and the corvée and the conscription fell at the same time on the registered households of Guanzhong and Guandong; the halving of the household registers by the end of the dynasty was already the consequence of this. Faced with such conditions, the common people turned the doctrine that Maitreya would appear as Shakyamuni declined, a teaching that had until then existed only in sutras and in the mouths of monks, into something that could be acted upon. The second level is the spread of Maitreya belief itself. Emperor Wen had issued bans during his reign on Maitreya teaching and on the forging of demonic writings, but the ban never took hold; by the Daye years commanderies and counties were keeping images of Maitreya, private copying of Maitreya sutras and the forming of associations had long ceased to be rare, and the Sui manuscripts and sutra copies excavated at Dunhuang document that trail in tangible form. The third level is the timing. On the first day of the first month the imperial carriage was to leave Luoyang for the western tour to Jiange, and the palace had to carry out the great audience and the whole ceremonial rearrangement of the progress; the watch at the Duan Gate, the armoury and the sequence of orders and messages were all at their tightest and most disturbed at that moment, and the attention of the guards was drawn towards the inner palace and the carriages. At the same time the first day of the year carried, in the popular reckoning, the sense that the old year had ended and a new one was about to begin, and images of calamity and replacement were easiest to kindle on such a day. The fourth level is the shape of the defence itself. The Duan Gate had a supervisor, soldiers and weapons; the institution was not short of men or of arms, but the working of the guard depended on obedience rather than on vigilance, and in the moment when the soldiers on duty bowed their heads before a religious slogan the entire system of the palace gate handed itself over at the moment it was most needed.
impact: 就眼前而言，這場事變的直接結果是零：端門沒有破，皇城沒有失守，壯士全滅，隋朝的統治秩序連一點裂痕都沒有顯露出來。但把時間拉長，意義並不為零。第一，它讓隋廷第一次看清，佛法在民間不只是一套教義，而是一種可以在宮門前變成武器的組織能力；第二，緊接而來的連坐千餘家，把一次失敗的奇襲放大成一次全國性的政治清理，州縣藉此攀比羅織，民間對朝廷的恐懼與對彌勒的期待同時加深——壓制往往製造它所壓制的東西。第三，它把西巡與內亂壓在同一個日子上，這本身就是一份診斷書：隋煬帝可以用大儀仗，可以接見西域二十七國的使臣，可以把自己打扮成天下共主，卻對自己腳下這座都城裡正在醞釀的東西一無所知，外部的秩序越堂皇，內部的資訊斷層就越深。第四，它把隋朝後半段的歷史推成一條清晰的線：從610年端門前的彌勒旗號，到大業九年楊玄感的起兵、大業十一年雁門之圍，再到大業十三年自號彌勒佛主的起事者，隋末的每一次大規模動亂都與民間對「新佛出世」的期待攪在一起，而這條線最終通向唐朝初年朝廷對彌勒信仰的長期警惕與禁斷。第五，就史料而言，這場事變只留下《資治通鑑》卷一百八十一隋紀五的一小段，以及後來條目化的記述。它太短促，沒有戰場，沒有戰報，卻因為記錄了洛陽皇城門禁的一個真實瞬間，成為觀察隋末洛陽的一個切口。
impactEn: In the immediate term the rising produced nothing: the Duan Gate did not fall, the imperial city was not breached, the intruders were wiped out, and not a crack appeared in the order of the Sui. But if the clock is stretched, the significance is not nil. First, it showed the Sui court for the first time that a Buddhist doctrine in the mouths of the people was not only a set of teachings but an organisational capacity that could turn into a weapon at a palace gate. Second, the more than a thousand households swept in afterwards turned a failed raid into a political purge of the whole state; commanderies and counties vied with one another in manufacturing cases, and the fear of the court among the people deepened at the same time as their expectation of Maitreya, for suppression tends to manufacture the very thing it is suppressing. Third, the western tour and the rising were pressed into the same day, and that in itself is a diagnosis: the Sui Yangdi could parade a great progress, could receive the envoys of the twenty-seven states of the Western Regions, could present himself as the universal sovereign, and yet know nothing of the thing fermenting under his feet in his own capital; the more lustrous the external order, the deeper the fissure in the flow of information inside. Fourth, it pushed the second half of the Sui into a single clear line: from the Maitreyan banner at the Duan Gate in 610, through the rising of Yang Xuanggan in the ninth year of Daye and the siege of Yanmen in the eleventh, to the insurgents who in the thirteenth year of Daye proclaimed themselves masters of Maitreya, every large disturbance of the late Sui was entangled with the popular expectation of a new Buddha, and that thread would eventually run into the long wariness of the Tang court towards Maitreya belief and its suppression. Fifth, as far as the sources are concerned, the affair survives as a short passage of the Comprehensive Mirror, book one hundred and eighty-one, and as a later encyclopaedic entry. It was too brief to leave a battlefield or a dispatch, but because it records one real moment of the guard at a gate of the Luoyang palace city, it has become a window through which the Luoyang of the late Sui can be looked at.
result: 結果可以分成軍事、刑事與政治三層。軍事上，壯士全部戰死在端門前，起事失敗，沒有一人進入皇城，沒有一處機關被毀，車駕的西巡照常出發。刑事上，隋煬帝下令在洛陽大索，搜索京師，把凡與彌勒有關的人一一緝拿，連坐者達千餘家；這道命令的落點從洛陽擴散到各州縣，其實施細、罪名與最終處分在史籍中沒有記載，只能知道牽連面極廣而手段極重。政治上，齊王楊暕的衛兵在事後立了功，他本人因此更受信任，而這份信任在隋末又成為另一重隱患——洛陽的權力在宇文化及弒君之後一度推向楊暕，而王世充與皇泰主楊侗的角力又把他推上又拉下。必須說清楚的是記載的空白：壯士的首領姓什麼、從哪裡來、籌劃了多久、是否另有內應、監門官與守門官軍事後如何處置、被連坐的千餘家最後怎樣結案，史籍一概不載。唯一可以肯定的是四點：事發在隋曆正月初一拂曉之前；地點是洛陽皇城建國門（端門）；起事以自稱彌勒佛的民間武裝形式出現並被當場殲滅；其後伴隨的是一場連坐千餘家的大搜捕。一場沒有戰場的戰役，留下的只有一座城門和一份很長的名單。
resultEn: The outcome divides into a military layer, a penal layer and a political layer. Militarily, the intruders were all killed in front of the Duan Gate, the rising failed, not one man entered the imperial city, no single mechanism was destroyed, and the western tour set out on its schedule. Penally, the Sui Yangdi ordered a great search of Luoyang, and the capital was combed for anyone connected with Maitreya; those arrested were carried off one by one, and the number of households drawn in through collective implication reached more than a thousand. The reach of that order spread from Luoyang to the commanderies and counties; the details of its execution, the charges and the final sentences have no record, and all that can be said is that the area of implication was very wide and the means very heavy. Politically, the household guard of Prince Qi Yang Jian had covered itself with glory and Yang himself was trusted more than before, and that trust was to become a different kind of danger at the end of the Sui, when the balance of power in Luoyang after Yuwen Huichi's killing of the emperor moved for a moment towards Yang Jian, and the struggle between Wang Shichong and the Prince of Yue Yang Tong pushed him up and then pulled him down. The gaps in the record must be stated plainly: what the leader of the intruders was called, where he came from, how long he had been planning, whether there was an accomplice inside, how the gate supervisor and the gate soldiers were dealt with afterwards, and how the more than a thousand households were closed out, none of it is recorded. Only four things can be established: it happened before dawn on the first day of the first month of the sixth year of Daye; it happened at the Jianguo Gate, the Duan Gate, of the imperial city of Luoyang; the rising took the form of armed townsmen calling themselves Maitreya and was annihilated on the spot; and what followed was a great purge implicating more than a thousand households. A battle without a battlefield leaves behind one gate and a very long list of names.
